stanzas.sanskrit:
वृकभृगुमुनिमोहिन्यम्बरीषादिवृत्ते-
-ष्वयि तव हि महत्त्वं सर्वशर्वादिजैत्रम् ।
स्थितमिह परमात्मन् निष्कलार्वागभिन्नं
किमपि यदवभातं तद्धि रूपं तवैव ॥ ९०-१ ॥
stanzas.commentary_en: From the stories of Vrikasuran, Bhrigu Muni, Mohini avathara and Ambarisha, it is evident that Bhagwan's glory rules over glory of all dieties including Parameshwaran. What is formless and still not any different from the form of Brahma, Vishnu and Shiva is the form of Bhagwan. It can be concluded that amongst the trinities, Lord Narayana/Hari/Krishna has the greatest glory.
stanzas.stanza_roman:
vṛkabhṛgumunimohinyambarīṣādivṛtte-
-ṣvayi tava hi mahattvaṃ sarvaśarvādijaitram |
sthitamiha paramātman niṣkalārvāgabhinnaṃ
kimapi yadavabhātaṃ taddhi rūpaṃ tavaiva || 90-1 ||

stanzas.sanskrit:
मूर्तित्रयेश्वरसदाशिवपञ्चकं यत्
प्राहुः परात्मवपुरेव सदाशिवोऽस्मिन् ।
तत्रेश्वरस्तु स विकुण्ठपदस्त्वमेव
त्रित्वं पुनर्भजसि सत्यपदे त्रिभागे ॥ ९०-२ ॥
stanzas.commentary_en: The Shaivaas speak of five aspects - Brahma, Vishnu, Shiva, Eshwara and Sadaashiva. Here Sadaashiva is Bhagwan HIMSELF, the Supreme Being. Bhagwan alone are Eshwara the Lord of Vaikuntha. The three forms of Trinity, Bhagwan alone assume in the three parts of Satyaloka.
stanzas.stanza_roman:
mūrtitrayeśvarasadāśivapañcakaṃ yat
prāhuḥ parātmavapureva sadāśivo’smin |
tatreśvarastu sa vikuṇṭhapadastvameva
tritvaṃ punarbhajasi satyapade tribhāge || 90-2 ||

stanzas.sanskrit:
तत्रापि सात्त्विकतनुं तव विष्णुमाहु-
-र्धाता तु सत्त्वविरलो रजसैव पूर्णः ।
सत्वोत्कटत्वमपि चास्ति तमोविकार-
-चेष्टादिकं च तव शङ्करनाम्नि मूर्तौ ॥ ९०-३ ॥
stanzas.commentary_en: In Trinities, the one who has maximum Sattvik qualities, is mentioned as Vishnu, one who possess Sattvik qualities but have more Rajasik qualities is called as Brahma and the one who has more Sattvik qualities but actions of Tamasik qualities is called as Shankaran.
stanzas.stanza_roman:
tatrāpi sāttvikatanuṃ tava viṣṇumāhu-
-rdhātā tu sattvaviralo rajasaiva pūrṇaḥ |
satvotkaṭatvamapi cāsti tamovikāra-
-ceṣṭādikaṃ ca tava śaṅkaranāmni mūrtau || 90-3 ||

stanzas.sanskrit:
तं च त्रिमूर्त्यतिगतं परपूरुषं त्वां
शर्वात्मनापि खलु सर्वमयत्वहेतोः ।
शंसन्त्युपासनविधौ तदपि स्वतस्तु
त्वद्रूपमित्यतिदृढं बहु नः प्रमाणम् ॥ ९०-४ ॥
stanzas.commentary_en: Transcending the Trinity, Bhagwan is considered Supreme and is the essence of all. Shaivas consider Parameshwaran as the one form of Lord and there are enough proofs in support of this truth.
stanzas.stanza_roman:
taṃ ca trimūrtyatigataṃ parapūruṣaṃ tvāṃ
śarvātmanāpi khalu sarvamayatvahetoḥ |
śaṃsantyupāsanavidhau tadapi svatastu
tvadrūpamityatidṛḍhaṃ bahu naḥ pramāṇam || 90-4 ||

stanzas.sanskrit:
श्रीशङ्करोऽपि भगवान् सकलेषु ताव-
-त्त्वामेव मानयति यो न हि पक्षपाती ।
त्वन्निष्ठमेव स हि नामसहस्रकादि-
-व्याख्यद्भवत् स्तुतिपरश्च गतिं गतोऽन्ते ॥ ९०-५ ॥
stanzas.commentary_en: Bhagawatpaada Sri Aadi Shankaraachaarya also, among all the Sakala forms, honours Vishnu form alone. He who is not of the nature of favouring any one deity has commented on the Sahasranaama etc., referring to Lord Vishnu alone. In the end he attained samaadhi singing Bhagwan praises.
stanzas.stanza_roman:
śrīśaṅkaro’pi bhagavān sakaleṣu tāva-
-ttvāmeva mānayati yo na hi pakṣapātī |
tvanniṣṭhameva sa hi nāmasahasrakādi-
-vyākhyadbhavat stutiparaśca gatiṃ gato’nte || 90-5 ||

stanzas.sanskrit:
मूर्तित्रयातिगमुवाच च मन्त्रशास्त्र-
-स्यादौ कलायसुषमं सकलेश्वरं त्वाम् ।
ध्यानम् च निष्कलमसौ प्रणवे खलूक्त्वा
त्वामेव तत्र सकलं निजगाद नाऽन्यम् ॥ ९०-६ ॥
stanzas.commentary_en: In his explanation about Manthra Sastras, Sri Adi Shankarachaarya has mentioned Lord Vishnu as supreme over the Trinity. He has described Lord Narayana as one appearing similar to a beautiful blue lily and one who is Lord of the universe, the Lord of all. When describing about Pranava, he has mentioned about Nishkala meditation on the Lord's supreme form only and not about forms of other deities.
stanzas.stanza_roman:
mūrtitrayātigamuvāca ca mantraśāstra-
-syādau kalāyasuṣamaṃ sakaleśvaraṃ tvām |
dhyānam ca niṣkalamasau praṇave khalūktvā
tvāmeva tatra sakalaṃ nijagāda nā’nyam || 90-6 ||

stanzas.sanskrit:
समस्तसारे च पुराणसङ्ग्रहे
विसंशयं त्वन्महिमैव वर्ण्यते ।
त्रिमूर्तियुक् सत्यपदत्रिभागतः
परं पदं ते कथितं न शूलिनः ॥ ९०-७ ॥
stanzas.commentary_en: In Purana sangraha, which summarizes all puranas, only Lord Narayana's glory has been explained. The Trimurti occupying the Satyaloka in three parts has been depicted. Vaikunta, where Lord Narayana/Hari/Krishna exists and it is more glorious and transcending than Satyaloka. There are no reference to the abode of Shiva.
stanzas.stanza_roman:
samastasāre ca purāṇasaṅgrahe
visaṃśayaṃ tvanmahimaiva varṇyate |
trimūrtiyuk satyapadatribhāgataḥ
paraṃ padaṃ te kathitaṃ na śūlinaḥ || 90-7 ||

stanzas.sanskrit:
यद्ब्राह्मकल्प इह भागवतद्वितीय-
-स्कन्धोदितं वपुरनावृतमीश धात्रे ।
तस्यैव नाम हरिशर्वमुखं जगाद
श्रीमाधवः शिवपरोऽपि पुराणसारे ॥ ९०-८ ॥
stanzas.commentary_en: At the time of Brahmakalpa, Bhagwan had revealed HIS form to Brahma, which is described in the second Skanda of the Bhaagavatam. Maadhavaachaarya, who was himself a votary of Shiva, has referred to that same form with the names Hari, Shiva etc., in Puraanasaara.
stanzas.stanza_roman:
yadbrāhmakalpa iha bhāgavatadvitīya-
-skandhoditaṃ vapuranāvṛtamīśa dhātre |
tasyaiva nāma hariśarvamukhaṃ jagāda
śrīmādhavaḥ śivaparo’pi purāṇasāre || 90-8 ||

stanzas.sanskrit:
ये स्वप्रकृत्यनुगुणा गिरिशं भजन्ते
तेषां फलं हि दृढयैव तदीयभक्त्या ।
व्यासो हि तेन कृतवानधिकारिहेतोः
स्कान्दादिकेषु तव हानिवचोऽर्थवादैः ॥ ९०-९ ॥
stanzas.commentary_en: People who by their instinct in previous births are devoted to Shiva and for such people, the liberation come through firm devotion to Shiva. While encouraging and motivating such persons, Sage Vyasa in Puranas like Skanda, has spoken about glory of Shiva more that of Lord Narayana.
stanzas.stanza_roman:
ye svaprakṛtyanuguṇā giriśaṃ bhajante
teṣāṃ phalaṃ hi dṛḍhayaiva tadīyabhaktyā |
vyāso hi tena kṛtavānadhikārihetoḥ
skāndādikeṣu tava hānivaco’rthavādaiḥ || 90-9 ||

stanzas.sanskrit:
भूतार्थकीर्तिरनुवादविरुद्धवादौ
त्रेधार्थवादगतयः खलु रोचनार्थाः ।
स्कान्दादिकेषु बहवोऽत्र विरुद्धवादा-
-स्त्वत्तामसत्वपरिभूत्युपशिक्षणाद्याः ॥ ९०-१० ॥
stanzas.commentary_en: Arthavaadam has three methods- 1) statements where existing facts are exaggerated, 2)statements are in accordance with experience, 3)statements are contrary to experience. These are used to make the subject matter interesting. In the Skanda Puraana and other scriptures there are many contrary statements, referring to Bhagwan’s Tamasik nature, Bhagwan’s defeat or Bhagwan being instructed by others etc., which are in the category of the third method.
stanzas.stanza_roman:
bhūtārthakīrtiranuvādaviruddhavādau
tredhārthavādagatayaḥ khalu rocanārthāḥ |
skāndādikeṣu bahavo’tra viruddhavādā-
-stvattāmasatvaparibhūtyupaśikṣaṇādyāḥ || 90-10 ||

stanzas.sanskrit:
यत्किञ्चिदप्यविदुषाऽपि विभो मयोक्तं
तन्मन्त्रशास्त्रवचनाद्यभिदृष्टमेव ।
व्यासोक्तिसारमयभागवतोपगीत
क्लेशान् विधूय कुरु भक्तिभरं परात्मन् ॥ ९०-११ ॥
stanzas.commentary_en: Bhattathiri mentioned at this context, that he is ignorant and what little he tried to say above, were the ones, which have been explained well in Manthra Sashtras. Even in the most significant Bhagavata purana, Sage Vyasa spoke glory of Lord Krishna. Bhattathiri worshipped Bhagwan to remove all his miseries and requested to make him more devoted to him.
stanzas.stanza_roman:
yatkiñcidapyaviduṣā’pi vibho mayoktaṃ
tanmantraśāstravacanādyabhidṛṣṭameva |
vyāsoktisāramayabhāgavatopagīta
kleśān vidhūya kuru bhaktibharaṃ parātman || 90-11 ||
